thread.title: Stock Market Update: Stock Market Puts Up Resilient Effort in the Face of Tariff Reminder

title: Stock Market Update: Stock Market Puts Up Resilient Effort in the Face of Tariff Reminder
text:
Stock Market Puts Up Resilient Effort in the Face of Tariff Reminder 27-Nov-18 13:00 ET Dow -75.28 at 24563.86, Nasdaq -21.73 at 7060.33, S&P -5.32 at 2668.27
[BRIEFING.COM] The S&P 500 takes a step back with a loss of 0.2% in what has been a seesaw session. The benchmark index has put up some resiliency efforts in the face of President Donald Trump rehashing a potential increase in Chinese tariffs, which dampened investor sentiment in the early morning.
Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average is down 0.3%, the Nasdaq Composite is down 0.3%, and the Russell 2000 is down 0.7%.
Specifically, President Trump said in a Wall Street Journal interview that it is "highly unlikely" he will refrain from raising a 10% tariff on $200 billion of Chinese goods to 25%, effective January 1. He added, too, that if China and the U.S. don't make a deal he will move ahead with a plan to place a tariff of 10% or 25% on an additional $267 billion of imported Chinese goods, which would possibly include iPhones and laptop computers.
Though the headlines aren't anything new, they have created some angst in the market over the idea that the G-20 meeting between might not produce a meaningful relaxation of trade tension between the two countries at the end of the week.
Apple (AAPL 172.64, -1.98, -1.1%) and the underperforming materials (-1.7%) and industrial (-1.0%) sectors have not reacted favorably to the tariff reminder. Stocks within these sectors are generally regarded as being more exposed to slower growth resulting from negative trade actions. Apple weighs on the heavily-weighted information technology group (-0.3%).
Industrials component United Tech (UTX 120.11, -7.87, -5.8%) weighs on the sector -- and the Dow -- as investors seem bothered by the cost associated with separating the company into three businesses, which will include the spin-off of the Otis and Carrier businesses. The decision comes after United Tech's recent acquisition of Rockwell Collins (COL 141.04, -0.59, -0.4%).
On the other hand, sectors that have provided some support for the broader market have been the utilities (+0.6%), communication services (+0.4%), and consumer staples (+0.4%) sectors. Communication component Netflix (NFLX 264.31, +2.88), up 1.0%, extends its gains from yesterday. In addition, chip stocks have also outperformed with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 0.2%.
Separately, U.S. Treasuries tick higher, pushing yields lower, with the benchmark 10-yr yield down two basis points to 3.05%. Also, the U.S. Dollar is up 0.3% to 97.40, and WTI crude stumbles 1.6% to $50.82/bbl after trading higher earlier.
Reviewing today's economic data, which included the Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index for November, the Case-Shiller 20-city Index for September, and the FHFA Housing Price Index for September: The Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index dipped to 135.7 in November (Briefing.com consensus 135.5) from 137.9 in October, which was the highest reading since September 2000. The key takeaway from the report is that consumer confidence remains at historically strong levels due in large part to positive views on the labor market. The Case-Shiller 10-city Index for September increased 5.1%, lower than the prior unrevised 5.5% increase in August. FHFA Housing Price Index for September increased 0.2%, lower than the revised 0.4% increase in August (from 0.3%).
